text: To find the eigenvalues of a triangular matrix, we remember that the determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of the entries on the diagonal. For instance, the following triangular matrix has the characteristic equation $$ \begin{aligned} \det\left( \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 4 \amp 2 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp -2 \amp -1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 3 \\ \end{array}\right] -\lambda I\right) \amp {}={} \det \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 4-\lambda \amp 2 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp -2-\lambda \amp -1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 3-\lambda \\ \end{array}\right] \\ \\ \amp {}={}(4-\lambda)(-2-\lambda)(3-\lambda) = 0\text{,} \end{aligned} $$ showing that the eigenvalues are the diagonal entries $\lambda = 4,-2,3$.
